status: One H264/AAC observation beats the saved VLC baseline in calibrated cycles, private RAM and dedicated GPU allocation. Raw CPU-time is nearly tied. O2 engine adopted for future repository builds.
method: Exactly one human-authorized visible Aperture launch, no discarded warmup and no VLC process. Fresh owned portable profile, SHA256-verified 180s 1080p30 H264/AAC stereo fixture, actual 1280x720 canvas at 96 DPI. Seven snapshots span the complete 29.9984629-second window after >=10s media time. Each baseline uses its own validated original calibration; CPU percent is one logical processor, divided by verified 24 for machine capacity. RAM and GPU allocations are snapshot medians; dedicated GPU memory is not GPU time. Passive thread counters are auxiliary; no intervals or observations were discarded.

cpuBurstReview.finding: The earlier O3 burst did not recur: all six new intervals are 4.11844–4.41444% of one logical processor. The full mean is 4.21460949%.
cpuBurstReview.cause: The old burst remains unexplained: its original run did not collect thread counters. A different profile/session without a burst cannot identify its cause or establish an O3 regression.
cpuBurstReview.threadFinding: 76 identities survive both endpoints; their cycle deltas equal 99.908% of the process delta with non-atomic timestamps. Largest observed threads: core, unnamed thread27472, vo. Window-owner UI thread is 0.18738 logical-processor percentage points of process-window CPU. Names are not stack attribution. Three identities disappear during the fourth interval; no counter-query errors.
cpuBurstReview.observerCost: Seven capture bounds are 3.6442–4.6493 ms. Observer runs in the host; process CPU totals remain primary. Instrumentation differs from the older VLC session.

decision.note: Validated O2 binary adopted in the repository for future builds. No new compilation claimed from the later default-profile edits. Desktop installation not touched, no app restarted, no release or upload. Existing features, CPU target, floating-point semantics and picture settings unchanged.
decision.reason: One explicitly authorized visible H264/AAC observation beat saved VLC in calibrated cycles and private RAM; raw CPU-time nearly tied. Earlier hidden native correctness and image checks passed. O2 is 2.709 MiB larger than size but 5.780 MiB smaller than O3. This is a practical bundle choice, not causal proof or a universal player ranking.

limits: One run per retained player session; six time intervals and seven RAM snapshots are not independent repeat runs. No stable cross-workload player ranking follows.

Calibrated cycles report 17.22% less CPU, but raw CPU-time accounting is 4.47940 versus 4.52952% of one logical processor, only 1.11% lower. Both retained; different counters and historical sessions limit confidence in the size of the CPU gain.
Saved VLC 3.0.23 from 2026-10-18T18:57:51.4393218Z reused unchanged; no new VLC measurement or baseline timestamp.
Aperture balanced filters differ from VLC linear; neither this visible run nor matching options prove identical decoder/pixels/presented-frame cadence or physical audio output.
Visible-window timing measures the bootstrap shell, not first visible video. Supplied runtime sizes differ in feature inventory; memory categories overlap and are not summed.
Earlier 80/80 native functional checks, 13 exact SDR frame cases and HDR fallback checks apply to this exact DLL hash, but retain their earlier dates and hidden-correctness scope.
The reused App EXE includes existing user changes; recording commit does not claim a clean rebuild. Only bundled native DLL/default build profile adopted. No install, restart, release or upload.
